svg.text: GUEST WING, TERRACED GARDENS & THE TIDE STAIR
South-west slope of the palace summit · citrus terraces, reflecting pool, tide baths, labyrinth and the private sea-cove
Dragonbound Cartographic Suite · Plate IV of IV
Drawn for the Autumn delegation · Vanserra household copy

g.text: SOUTH COLONNADE OF THE STATE WING · Plate III ↑
white sand · no path but the stair
no descent east of the cove
The evening flood covers seven treads,
Sea-lounge, open to the bay; rooms connect
Bougainvillea bower — screened seat for two
Wisteria pergola under the retaining wall
Pool Pavilion — domed tholos on the point
The Cascade, falling to the sea
Hot room over a banked fire-bowl
canon = from the books · ⚑ = devised for this table
◆ Four levels, twenty-two metres. Each terrace hides the one below it from the
palace. Only the parterre and the middle of the citrus rows lie under the
◆ The guest wing. Linked rooms round a lounge open to the sea, as Summer
lodges visiting courts. A late-arriving emissary would be put here, a short walk
◆ To be seen walking. The parterre and the pool are where the court strolls
before dinner. A pair pacing the cypress allée is visible, proper and out of
◆ To talk unheard. The bougainvillea bower, the shuttered Lemon Pavilion, and
the heart of the labyrinth, where head-high myrtle swallows a voice at six paces.
◆ The quiet way. Service stair, east steps, behind the Lemon Pavilion, round the
baths and the labyrinth hedge: from the colonnade to the Tide Stair without
◆ The Tide Stair. Rock-cut, twenty-four treads, the last seven under water at the
flood. It is the only way to the cove, and the only way back passes the
sea-garden in full view of anyone at the whisper bench.
◆ By water. A skiff in the grotto reaches the west cliff below the Salt-Arch in a
quarter-hour at slack tide; the Teeth lie beyond.
◆ After dark. Only the parterre lanterns and the pavilion dome are lit. The lower
terraces, the labyrinth and the stair keep no lamps.
